Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old Adriana Katherine with 3-day history of worsening headache (generalized, right periorbital predominance), photophobia, and brief visual phenomena (“shooting lights”) with nausea (no vomiting); clinical impression of migraine. Management discussed: optimize analgesia (NSAIDs, acetaminophen/codeine), headache diary, safety-net advice, and follow-up in 1–2 weeks; consider prophylaxis if recurrent.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache for ~3 days.
- Onset/Timeline:
  - Began at work ~3 days ago; worsened by end of day 1 and further worsened the next morning.
  - Persistent headache with fluctuating intensity; overall worsening over 3 days.
- Character:
  - Location: All over head, worse around right eye.
  - Quality: Dull with intermittent sharper pains.
  - Severity: 8/10.
  - Course: Gradual onset; continuous with exacerbations.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Photophobia (hurts to look at bright lights).
  - Visual phenomena at onset (“shooting lights”).
  - Nausea (“feel sick”) without vomiting.
  - Difficulty focusing.
  - Denies vision loss; no reported blurry vision.
  - Denies speech difficulty; denies limb weakness.
  - Denies recent head injury, fever, or rash.
  - Neck pain/stiffness: patient said “Yeah,” then “No” (conflict noted).
- Prior episodes: Has had headaches before that typically resolve with ibuprofen; current episode not improving with ibuprofen.
- Triggers/Factors: Works extensively on computers; reduced screen brightness. Mild work stress (new project). Hydration considered by patient but not confirmed as cause.

Past Medical History:
- No other medical conditions reported.
- No personal history of migraine.

Medications:
- Regular medications: None reported.
- Recent self-treatment: Ibuprofen, 3 tablets/day for last 2 days; strength and route not documented; ineffective.
- Proposed/Discussed by clinician:
  - Naproxen (prescription discussed; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Acetaminophen (paracetamol) or codeine as adjuncts (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies (per patient).

Social History:
- Living situation: Shares home with three housemates (total four people).
- Occupation: Works in IT; extensive computer use; reduced screen brightness due to symptoms.
- Vision: Wears glasses since age 5; no recent eye exam.
- Stress: Some increased stress due to new project; not beyond usual.
- Tobacco: Social smoker.
- Alcohol: Drinks socially.
- Contraception: Asked if on the pill; response not documented.

Family History:
- Mother and sister with migraines.
  - Sister: infrequent.
  - Mother: frequent; worse with seasonal changes; can be incapacitating for a few days.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented.
- Vitals: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None ordered or documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute headache consistent with migraine (photophobia, possible visual aura, nausea; family history; no focal deficits reported).
  - Optimize NSAID use: Advised that ibuprofen can be taken up to two tablets three times daily (tablet strength not documented).
  - Plan to prescribe naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - May add acetaminophen (paracetamol) or codeine as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Keep a headache diary to identify potential triggers.
  - Follow-up in 1–2 weeks.
  - Safety-net: Return or call sooner if headaches worsen or do not improve, or if new symptoms occur (vision problems, limb weakness, feeling unwell).
  - Consider prophylactic therapy if headaches become frequent; to be discussed at follow-up.
- Issue 2: Photophobia/possible eye strain with prolonged computer use; longstanding corrective lenses; no recent eye exam.
  - Recommendation: Arrange an eye test.

General Plan items:
- Off-work adjustments as needed; reduce screen brightness (already implemented by patient).

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals, full neurologic exam (cranial nerves, motor/sensory, coordination/gait), fundoscopic exam, pregnancy status, response to contraception question, detailed dosing/route for proposed medications, comprehensive medication reconciliation.
- Internal conflicts: Neck pain/stiffness—patient said “Yeah” then “No” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Occasional disfluencies/pauses; overall key clinical details captured.
